edges.description: Polygenic liability is placed upstream of the diagnostic psychopathology, but the intervening developmental, molecular, and neural mechanisms are unresolved.
Fear of weight gain, body-image disturbance, and persistent weight-gain-interfering behavior are expressed clinically as restrictive eating and related abnormal eating behavior.
AN psychopathology motivates severe dietary restriction and other weight-loss behavior.
Sustained energy restriction reduces body mass and produces chronic undernutrition.
Electrolyte and volume abnormalities are context dependent and are not universal; purging and water-loading behaviors can substantially modify risk.
intermediate_mechanisms: Purging, polydipsia, reduced intake, and renal adaptation

edges.description: The malnourished low-energy state is expressed clinically as decreased body weight, often following substantial or rapid weight loss.
edges.target: Low Body Weight and Weight Loss

edges.description: Loss of adipose tissue and reduced energy intake lower the adipocyte-derived hormone leptin, producing the hypoleptinemia that signals the starved state.
Chronic starvation elicits adaptive and maladaptive changes across gonadal, growth-hormone, adrenal, thyroid, and appetite-hormone axes.
intermediate_mechanisms: Hypothalamic-pituitary axis adaptation to chronic energy deficit

edges.description: Recent and rapid weight loss contributes to bradycardia and broader cardiovascular instability.
intermediate_mechanisms: Autonomic adaptation, reduced cardiac mass, and electrolyte disturbance

edges.description: Disordered eating and malnutrition produce delayed gastric emptying and constipation that can complicate refeeding.
A substantial component of widespread brain structural differences is associated with acute undernutrition and is smaller after partial weight restoration.
intermediate_mechanisms: Acute undernutrition and lower body mass index

edges.description: Hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction suppresses gonadal hormone signaling.
Starvation-related endocrine changes and altered body composition impair bone accrual and maintenance.
intermediate_mechanisms: Low gonadal steroids, growth-hormone resistance, hypercortisolemia, and low body mass

edges.description: Suppression of reproductive endocrine signaling can result in hypothalamic amenorrhea.
intermediate_mechanisms: Reduced hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal signaling and low gonadal steroids

edges.description: Impaired bone integrity is measured clinically as reduced bone mineral density across total body, spine, hip, and femur sites.
Recent and rapid weight loss is strongly associated with severe bradycardia in hospitalized adolescents.
AN can confer arrhythmia risk through several cardiac and electrolyte pathways.
intermediate_mechanisms: Myocardial structural change, conduction disturbance, and electrolyte imbalance

edges.description: Potassium depletion can occur, particularly with purging behaviors.
Sodium disturbance can occur through reduced intake, volume regulation, or excessive water intake.
Electrolyte imbalance can amplify arrhythmia risk, especially in medically unstable or purging presentations.
Gastrointestinal dysmotility manifests clinically as constipation.

Hypoleptinemia removes a permissive signal for the reproductive axis, contributing to hypothalamic hypogonadism and amenorrhea; this is the leptin-specific mediator of the broader endocrine starvation response.
intermediate_mechanisms: Loss of leptin's permissive signal for hypothalamic GnRH / HPG-axis activity

edges.description: Low leptin is hypothesized to drive starvation-induced hyperactivity; the causal step is established in the ABA rodent model (via VTA STAT3 signaling) but only correlational (inverted-U) in humans, so this edge is carried under an emerging hypothesis rather than as an established human mechanism.
intermediate_mechanisms: Leptin signal transduction via STAT3 in ventral tegmental area (VTA) dopaminergic neurons (demonstrated in the activity-based anorexia model)

edges.description: Low serum leptin is a direct readout of the Hypoleptinemia mechanism node and indexes the severity of the starvation-adaptation state; it partially normalizes with weight restoration and is the pharmacodynamic target of metreleptin substitution.

nodes.description: Persistent restriction and other behavior that interferes with weight gain are core diagnostic manifestations. Fear of weight gain and body-image disturbance are retained in the clinical description because the available HPO term is broader than the full psychiatric construct.

evidence.reference_title: A Feasibility Trial of Theta Burst Stimulation in Anorexia Nervosa (AN)
evidence.snippet: Anorexia Nervosa (AN) is a life-threatening eating disorder characterised by an intense fear of weight gain and disturbed body image, which motivates severe dietary restriction or other weight loss behaviours (e.g. purging).

nodes.description: Hypothalamic amenorrhea can occur in postmenarchal patients with AN. It is a consequence of energy-deficit-associated reproductive-axis suppression and is not required for diagnosis; it does not apply to all sexes or life stages.

evidence.reference_title: Associations between bone mineral density, body composition and amenorrhoea in females with eating disorders: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
evidence.snippet: In AN, low weight, hypothalamic amenorrhoea, and longer illness duration are established risk factors for low BMD

nodes.description: Arrhythmias are potentially serious complications of AN, mediated through cardiac structural, conduction, autonomic, and electrolyte pathways.

evidence.reference_title: Medical complications of anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa.
evidence.snippet: Acrocyanosis is common, and patients with anorexia nervosa are at risk of various arrhythmias.

nodes.description: Bradycardia is common in medically unstable, recently weight-losing adolescents and may prompt hospitalization; the cohort estimate below is specific to hospitalized adolescents and is not a population frequency.

evidence.reference_title: Determinants of severe bradycardia in adolescents hospitalized for anorexia nervosa.
evidence.snippet: Forty-eight percent of the AN patient admissions were due to severe bradycardia (AN-B+ group).

nodes.description: Weight loss, autonomic adaptation, reduced cardiac mass, and electrolyte disturbances contribute to bradycardia, conduction disturbance, and arrhythmia risk. Not every patient has the same cardiovascular phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: Incidence and Risk of Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients With Anorexia Nervosa
evidence.snippet: Compared with the control group, the AN group had significantly higher risks of MACE (adjusted HR [AHR], 3.78; 95% CI, 2.83-5.05) and any cardiovascular condition (AHR, 1.93; 95% CI, 1.54-2.41).

nodes.description: Constipation and delayed gastric emptying occur in both AN presentations, often improve with nutritional recovery, and may complicate refeeding.

evidence.reference_title: Gastrointestinal disturbances in eating disorders: clinical and neurobiological aspects.
evidence.snippet: Both anorexia nervosa subtypes experience substantial delays in gastric emptying as well as constipation.

nodes.description: Depression is a frequent and clinically important psychiatric comorbidity; cross-sectional association does not establish directionality.

evidence.reference_title: Eating Disorders: A Review.
evidence.snippet: Individuals with anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa, and binge-eating disorder have high lifetime rates of depression (76.3% for bulimia nervosa, 65.5% for binge-eating disorder, and 49.5% for anorexia nervosa) and higher rates of suicide attempts than those without eating disorders.

nodes.description: Eating-disorder-focused CBT is one of several recommended psychotherapies. Selection depends on age, illness duration, comorbidity, prior treatment, and patient preference; it is not presented as uniformly superior.

evidence.reference_title: Anorexia nervosa—an update
evidence.snippet: The treatment of choice for AN includes cognitive behavioral therapy and family-based therapy for children and adolescents.

nodes.description: Restriction, purging, polydipsia, and renal adaptation can produce electrolyte and volume abnormalities. These are severity- and behavior-dependent complications rather than universal diagnostic signs.

evidence.reference_title: Medical complications of anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa.
evidence.snippet: Nutritional abnormalities are also common, including sodium depletion and hypovolemia, hypophosphatemia and hypomagnesemia.

nodes.description: Physical hyperactivity, motor restlessness, and a driven urge to exercise are common in acute AN and correlate inversely with serum leptin; they are modeled here as a leptin-linked behavioral manifestation (see the leptin_hyperactivity mechanistic hypothesis). HP:0000752 (Hyperactivity) is the closest available HPO term but is anchored to ADHD-type motor/attentional hyperactivity; the preferred_term carries the AN-specific compulsive, starvation-driven-exercise nuance the ontology class does not yet capture.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical Trials Required to Assess Potential Benefits and Side Effects of Treatment of Patients With Anorexia Nervosa With Recombinant Human Leptin.
evidence.snippet: an inverted U-shaped relationship has been observed between their serum leptin levels and physical activity.

nodes.description: Family-based treatment with parental oversight of eating has the strongest comparative evidence in youth with AN. The age context is essential and the result should not be generalized to all adults or severe enduring illness.

evidence.reference_title: Eating Disorders: A Review.
evidence.snippet: Youth with anorexia nervosa benefit from family-based treatment with parental oversight of eating, resulting in a remission rate at 6 to 12 months of 48.6% vs 34.3% with individual treatment (odds ratio, 2.08; 95% CI, 1.07-4.03; P = .03).

nodes.description: Delayed gastric emptying and constipation occur in both AN presentations and can make nutritional rehabilitation uncomfortable; most changes improve with restoration of normal intake and body weight.

evidence.reference_title: Gastrointestinal disturbances in eating disorders: clinical and neurobiological aspects.
evidence.snippet: Gastrointestinal disturbances develop secondary to the disordered eating behaviour and the concomitant malnutrition and subside mostly with the resumption of normal food intake and body weight.

nodes.description: Energy-deficit-associated hypothalamic-pituitary suppression reduces gonadal hormones. Amenorrhea is an important manifestation in some postmenarchal patients but is not required for a modern AN diagnosis.

evidence.reference_title: The endocrine manifestations of anorexia nervosa: mechanisms and management.
evidence.snippet: Dysfunction of the hypothalamic-pituitary axis includes hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with relative oestrogen and androgen deficiency

nodes.description: Hypokalemia can occur, particularly with purging or other fluid-loss behaviors, but is not universal across AN presentations.

evidence.reference_title: Eating Disorders: A Review.
evidence.snippet: These disorders may be associated with changes in weight, electrolyte abnormalities (eg, hyponatremia, hypokalemia), bradycardia, disturbances in reproductive hormones (eg, decreased estradiol levels in females), and decreased bone density.

evidence.reference_title: Does hypoleptinemia trigger entrapment in anorexia nervosa? Etiological and clinical considerations.
evidence.snippet: Hypoleptinemia as a core endocrine feature of AN serves as a central and peripheral trigger of tissue-specific adaptations to starvation.

readouts.interpretation: Low serum leptin is a direct readout of the Hypoleptinemia mechanism node and indexes the severity of the starvation-adaptation state; it partially normalizes with weight restoration and is the pharmacodynamic target of metreleptin substitution.

meta.specificity: Low for AN as a stand-alone diagnostic marker (reflects low fat mass generally); high as an index of the acute starvation-adaptation state.

nodes.description: Hyponatremia can occur through water-loading behavior, reduced intake, or altered volume regulation and requires context-specific interpretation.

evidence.reference_title: The endocrine manifestations of anorexia nervosa: mechanisms and management.
evidence.snippet: Dysfunction of the hypothalamic-pituitary axis includes hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with relative oestrogen and androgen deficiency, growth hormone resistance, hypercortisolaemia, non-thyroidal illness syndrome, hyponatraemia and hypooxytocinaemia.

nodes.description: Hospital-level supportive care is indicated for serious medical or psychiatric complications such as severe bradycardia or suicidality. Admission decisions are individualized; this entry does not define bedside thresholds.

evidence.reference_title: Eating Disorders: A Review.
evidence.snippet: Individuals with serious medical or psychiatric complications of eating disorders such as bradycardia or suicidality should be hospitalized for treatment.

nodes.description: Significantly low body weight is a defining state. Recent weight loss can carry medical risk even before an extremely low absolute weight is reached.
nodes.id: Low Body Weight and Weight Loss

evidence.reference_title: Determinants of severe bradycardia in adolescents hospitalized for anorexia nervosa.
evidence.snippet: Patients in this group had a higher maximum lifetime weight (P = 0.0045), greater premorbid weight loss (P = 0.0011), and more rapid weight loss (P = 0.0001).

nodes.description: The low-energy state is the established proximal driver of many endocrine, cardiovascular, gastrointestinal, skeletal, and brain-state consequences. It should not be mistaken for evidence that those downstream changes caused the initial psychiatric syndrome.

evidence.reference_title: The endocrine manifestations of anorexia nervosa: mechanisms and management.
evidence.snippet: Anorexia nervosa is a psychiatric disorder characterized by altered body image, persistent food restriction and low body weight, and is associated with global endocrine dysregulation in both adolescent girls and women.

nodes.description: Metreleptin, a recombinant human leptin analogue, has been used off-label in small uncontrolled case series of severely ill, hyperactive patients with AN, with reports of rapid improvement in depression, eating-disorder cognitions, weight phobia, and hyperactivity. It is a mechanism-directed substitution for the hypoleptinemia of AN. It is NOT approved for AN (metreleptin is approved only for generalized lipodystrophy); the evidence is uncontrolled and the authors uniformly call for randomized placebo-controlled trials.

evidence.reference_title: Short-term metreleptin treatment of patients with anorexia nervosa: rapid on-set of beneficial cognitive, emotional, and behavioral effects.
evidence.snippet: Surprisingly, depression improved rapidly in all patients.

evidence.reference_title: Rapid Emergence of Appetite and Hunger Resulting in Weight Gain and Improvement of Eating Disorder Symptomatology during and after Short-Term Off-Label Metreleptin Treatment of a Patient with Anorexia Nervosa.
evidence.snippet: was associated with self-reported increments of appetite and hunger resulting in rapid weight gain and substantial improvement of eating disorder cognitions and of depression.

evidence.reference_title: Rapid amelioration of anorexia nervosa in a male adolescent during metreleptin treatment including recovery from hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.
evidence.snippet: underscore the need for a double-blind placebo-controlled trial to confirm the observed strong, multiple and rapid onset beneficial effects of metreleptin in AN.

evidence.reference_title: Suggestive Evidence for an Antidepressant Effect of Metreleptin Treatment in Patients with Lipodystrophy.
evidence.snippet: depression in anorexia nervosa (AN), which is also characterized by hypoleptinemia, improves substantially upon treatment with metreleptin

evidence.reference_title: Case report: clinical improvements observed in first off-label metreleptin treatment of a patient with atypical anorexia nervosa.
evidence.snippet: Randomized controlled trials are warranted for both eating disorders.

nodes.description: Nutritional support and gradual, monitored weight restoration address the low-energy state and medical complications. Refeeding intensity and electrolyte monitoring must be individualized because severely malnourished patients can decompensate during refeeding; DisMech does not prescribe a patient-level protocol.
nodes.id: Nutritional rehabilitation and monitored weight restoration

evidence.reference_title: Eating Disorders: A Review.
evidence.snippet: First-line treatments for eating disorders include nutritional support, psychotherapy, and pharmacotherapy.

nodes.description: Olanzapine may be considered as an adjunct for weight gain in selected patients. Evidence is moderate, it is not a stand-alone treatment, and broad psychopharmacotherapy efficacy in AN has not been established.

evidence.reference_title: Anorexia nervosa—an update
evidence.snippet: With the exception of moderate evidence supporting the use of olanzapine regarding weight gain, there is currently no evidence for the efficacy of psychopharmacotherapy in AN.

nodes.description: Common germline variation contributes distributed susceptibility across psychiatric and metabolic trait domains. The node does not assert a single causal gene or a known molecular route to AN.

evidence.reference_title: Genome-wide association study identifies eight risk loci and implicates metabo-psychiatric origins for anorexia nervosa.
evidence.snippet: These results further encourage a reconceptualization of anorexia nervosa as a metabo-psychiatric disorder.

nodes.description: Reduced bone mineral density is a major long-term complication, especially in women with low body mass, altered body composition, and amenorrhea; the evidence base cited here is predominantly female.

evidence.reference_title: Associations between bone mineral density, body composition and amenorrhoea in females with eating disorders: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
evidence.snippet: BMD in individuals with AN (total body, spine, hip, and femur), with BN (total body and spine) and with OSFED (spine) was lower than in HC.

nodes.description: Fear of weight gain, disturbance in body-weight or shape experience, and persistent weight-gain-interfering behavior motivate restriction. This clinical state is established; its upstream molecular and circuit causes remain incompletely resolved.

evidence.reference_title: A Feasibility Trial of Theta Burst Stimulation in Anorexia Nervosa (AN)
evidence.snippet: Anorexia Nervosa (AN) is a life-threatening eating disorder characterised by an intense fear of weight gain and disturbed body image, which motivates severe dietary restriction or other weight loss behaviours (e.g. purging).

nodes.description: Low body mass, low fat and lean mass, amenorrhea, and endocrine adaptation reduce bone mineral density and increase later osteoporosis and fracture risk.

evidence.reference_title: Associations between bone mineral density, body composition and amenorrhoea in females with eating disorders: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
evidence.snippet: Lower bone mineral density (BMD) increases the risk of osteoporosis in individuals with eating disorders (EDs), particularly women with anorexia nervosa (AN), making them susceptible to pain and fractures throughout adulthood.

nodes.description: Chronic low energy alters hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal, growth-hormone, adrenal, thyroid, leptin, ghrelin, and related endocrine axes. Many changes are adaptive to starvation, not validated diagnostic biomarkers.

evidence.reference_title: Peripheral Biomarkers of Anorexia Nervosa: A Meta-Analysis
evidence.snippet: Our findings indicate that peripheral biomarkers may be linked to the pathophysiology of AN, such as processes of adaptation to starvation.

nodes.description: Persistent caloric restriction creates negative energy balance; in the binge-eating/purging presentation, vomiting or other compensatory behaviors can add fluid and electrolyte losses.

evidence.reference_title: A Feasibility Trial of Theta Burst Stimulation in Anorexia Nervosa (AN)
evidence.snippet: Anorexia Nervosa (AN) is a life-threatening eating disorder characterised by an intense fear of weight gain and disturbed body image, which motivates severe dietary restriction or other weight loss behaviours (e.g. purging).

nodes.description: Acute AN is associated with widespread reductions in cortical thickness and subcortical volume. Their relationship to low BMI and attenuation after partial weight restoration make them important state markers but not proof of a primary neural cause.

evidence.reference_title: Brain Structure in Acutely Underweight and Partially Weight-Restored Individuals With Anorexia Nervosa: A Coordinated Analysis by the ENIGMA Eating Disorders Working Group.
evidence.snippet: In AN, reductions in cortical thickness, subcortical volumes, and, to a lesser extent, cortical surface area were sizable (Cohen's d up to 0.95), widespread, and colocalized with hub regions.
